actual_scope: Determine the exact scale-uniform infimum of the inverse Euclidean norm of every finite normalized Gaussian section at either half-shift endpoint.
scope_change_reason: An original analytic side result takes the finite-cap sharpness question of Jose Manuel / PR4193. No selected assumption is audited or discharged.
bottleneck_link: The lower envelope shows that no scale-uniform constant or sublinear size allowance can replace the linear half-shift inverse budget. Production normalization, gauges and complete costs remain separate.
stop_rule: Ship the first proved and exactly corroborated envelope; leave fixed-q constants, interior crossover and physical integration open.
evidence: Written proof and exact finite corroboration: 80 literal endpoint inverses, 2040 entries, 70 strict cases, 32 complete Laurent identities, eight triangular inverse pairs, 28 small-scale matrices, 21 error comparisons, ten rejected inputs and five semantic controls.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: What is the sharp leading coefficient at a fixed positive q as N grows?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The exact infimum over q does not determine the norm at a fixed Gaussian scale.
open_questions.first_step: Study the positive inverse in the bulk upper triangle and bound its difference from a constant multiple of U_N in operator norm.
open_questions.blocked_by: A uniform bound on boundary and near-diagonal contributions, with q fixed.

open_questions.question: What finite-size lower envelope holds for shifts approaching but not equal to one half?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Interior shifts can have a size-independent inverse allowance, unlike the endpoints.
open_questions.first_step: Retain the decaying geometric triangle under the exact diagonal conjugation and identify its largest singular value.
open_questions.blocked_by: A sharp two-parameter bound and a justified limit regime; no interior claim is made here.
